newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down, but spot tightness lingers.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down, but spot tightness lingers.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended lower apart from spot November which nudged higher, continued testimony to the short-term tightness, traders and analysts said.
Some expected the market to have improved in the absence of delivery notices Monday. The open interest in November is still 4,666 lots. The contract expires on November 10.
Bernard Savaiko of PaineWebber said the technical picture for most-active January looked terrible, with rally attempts turned back.
The weak picture was a continuation from the USDA's October crop report which forecast a bigger crop, Savaiko added. "Inventories are a little bit low but the perception is that they will pick up."

January orange juice settled 1.85 cents lower at 97.35 cents per pound, a fresh life-of-contract low. January was traded 99.55 to 97.10 cents. November went out 0.30 cent firmer at 107.10 cents, a wide ten cent premium over January.
